transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-15 16:30 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Redwood CSM); Lina Gomez (CTO, Acme Analytics), Raj Patel (Eng Lead), Asha Verma (ML Engineer), Tom Nguyen (SRE)

Summary: quick discovery for PLG/self-serve quickstart; want to validate time-to-first-token, free credits, and get pilot running; evaluate hosted vs dedicated for anticipated production load; security / SOC2 / VPC questions.

00:00 Lina: okay, thanks for setting this up, we wanted to walk through the quickstart and understand how fast we can get something live with Redwood hosted API, and, um, what the path looks like if we need Dedicated or Private later.
00:18 Jamie: sure, hi everyone, I'm Jamie, AE on the account; Marcus is our solutions engineer; we'll cover the quickstart flow, free credits, and typical pilot steps. Quick question before we start: is your initial goal to prototype in 1-2 weeks or is this more of a spike?
00:31 Lina: prototype in two weeks ideally — get a small proof of concept that generates summaries and embeddings for a subset of our product data, then we can evaluate costs and latencies.
00:44 Marcus: great, that aligns with what we've seen — for a quickstart we usually get customers to first-token in under an hour: sign up, take free credits, run a curl or SDK call, then a small benchmark run. We have a quickstart doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart and a sample repo, I can share.
01:02 Raj: can you remind us what the free credits look like? Also curious about token pricing and cost model for hosted.
01:08 Jamie: yes — free credits for PLG signups (we give a starter pool, enough for several thousand tokens); hosted pricing is usage-based per token and per embedding unit, we'll share the exact numbers in the follow-up; for pilots we often discuss limited Dedicated trial if predictable throughput is needed.
01:28 Tom: our main concern is latency — p50 around 150ms for short responses is what we shoot for. Can hosted hit that?
01:36 Marcus: depends on model and sequence length — for smaller models and streaming off the hosted API, p50 under 150ms is achievable for short prompts; we recommend running a quick perf test against your prompt templates. For sustained low-latency at 100s of qps, Dedicated pools help.
01:58 Asha: what's the SDK experience? We mostly use Python and Node.
02:04 Marcus: we have first-party SDKs for Python/Node and curl examples; typical flow: install SDK, export API key, run a quick generate call. Example snippet we handed many folks: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"rw-mistral-7b","prompt":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":60}'
02:23 Raj: ok great. How is auth handled — can we SSO to manage keys?
02:28 Jamie: yes — for enterprise we support SSO/SAML, RBAC and org-level API key management; in the quickstart you'll use a personal API key. For production we recommend scoped service keys and per-route quotas.
02:44 Lina: security is big for us — SOC 2? KMS? Audit logs?
02:49 Marcus: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we provide audit logs, integrations with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments, and detailed access controls. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit; Private includes VPC options and KMS. I'll attach our security pack.
03:03 Raj: perfect. For the pilot we plan to ingest product tickets with variable length. Sequence lengths can be up to ~1,200 tokens, avg 220. Any special guidance?
03:14 Marcus: for that distribution you should consider chunking and embeddings for retrieval-augmented generation; also quantization/model selection matters — we can recommend model variants tuned for longer contexts. Caching prefixes also helps reduce cost if prompts share context.
03:31 Asha: cost: is there a quick way to estimate unit economics?
03:35 Jamie: yes we have a cost estimator spreadsheet; Marcus can run a quick estimation once we know token counts and expected qps. For the pilot we'll run a small benchmark and give projected cost per 1M tokens.
03:50 Tom: what about private data — does hosted ever see PII? We need controls for retention and purge policies.
03:58 Marcus: hosted can be configured for no-logging/short retention for enterprise customers; Dedicated and Private give stronger isolation. We also support customer-managed retention policies and contract terms.
04:15 Lina: timeline — if we spin up a quickstart today, how long till we have something we can demo to the product team?
04:22 Jamie: typically under a day to prototype and a week for a polished demo; we'll help with sample prompts and evaluation harness.
04:31 Raj: ok let's talk specifics — what do you need from us to enable a quickstart?
04:36 Marcus: ideally: sample prompts, small dataset (a few hundred docs), and expected QPS; plus an owner for the pilot (Lina?). We'll give a benchmark script and a config for the SDK.
04:47 Lina: I'll be the owner. We'll give you a 500-doc sample and target metrics: p50 <=150ms, p95 <=400ms, and cost target around $0.0015-0.002/token depending on model.
05:02 Jamie: noted. We'll propose a 2-week pilot: week 1 - quickstart + smoke tests, week 2 - benchmarking and model tuning. After that we can discuss Dedicated if throughput or QoS needs require it.
05:17 Raj: what are failure modes? Do you do automatic fallbacks if a model is overloaded?
05:23 Marcus: yes — smart routing with fallbacks to compatible variants, and canary rollouts; for Dedicated you get reserved capacity and autoscaling policies. We'll show the routing doc in the follow-up.
05:36 Asha: one more — do you support embeddings and vector store integrations out of the box?
05:41 Jamie: yes, embeddings API, direct connectors for common vector DBs and sample code for FAISS/Weaviate. We'll send those links.
05:53 Tom: For the quickstart, will the sample repo include a simple benchmark that measures latency p50/p95 and token counts?
05:59 Marcus: yes, the repo includes a bench runner that hits the live API and outputs latency histograms and token counts; we'll tailor it to your sequence length distribution.
06:12 Lina: any blockers on our side? We need to resolve security expectations and get the pilot funding approved.
06:18 Jamie: understood. For security, Marcus will attach SOC2 and the security pack. For funding, we'll keep pilot low-cost using free credits and a small usage cap; once you like results we can discuss Dedicated quoting.
06:32 Raj: competitive question — other teams are looking at Anthropic/Claude and OpenAI; what's the advantage here?
06:39 Jamie: typically cost and deployment flexibility — Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private; for teams that value on-prem or VPC options and stronger cost controls, that's a differentiator. We also emphasize observability and per-request cost telemetry.
06:58 Asha: transcript quality note — sorry if there are mis-words, we were on a bit of a lag.
07:04 Marcus: no worries. Next steps recap: Jamie will send quickstart link and free credits details; Marcus will share benchmark script and security pack; Lina to confirm pilot goals and sample dataset.
07:18 Jamie: we'll aim to have the quickstart materials and credits email by tomorrow (2026-03-16). Marcus will follow up with the bench script by 2026-03-18. Lina, if you can confirm the dataset and goals by 2026-03-19 we can kick off the pilot week of 2026-03-23.
07:35 Lina: sounds good. Thanks everyone.
07:39 Meeting end.
